newsitem.title: THAILAND: First quarter finance results shake Thai bourse.
newsitem.headline: First quarter finance results shake Thai bourse.

text.p: Although battered Thai finance firms on Monday posted poor first quarter results as expected, the sharp drop in the figures still caused the jittery bourse to fall, analysts and brokers said.
First quarter results of about half the major finance and securities firms were reported on Monday, and most came in as expected -- with large declines and some red ink.
"It's red, but they're bound to be red. Everyone knew the numbers would be horrendous," said one analyst.
Although most analysts said they had expected companies in Thailand's beleaguered finance sector to show poor first quarter results, the slew of lower numbers brought the bourse down.

"There is still very much of a retail base here," said an analyst. "In the Thai market you often see this. People who follow closely know what will happen but there are still others who just react to what they see -- so the market goes down."
The Stock Exchange of Thailand composite index dropped 6.02 points to end at 694.21. Finance counters fell 1.7 percent.

Among the larger finance firms, Asia Credit Plc posted a profit of 95.44 million baht ($3.67 million) compared to a net of 276.89 million the same period last year. Dhana Siam Finance and Securities Plc slid to 85.79 million baht from 353.6 million and Krungthai Thanakit Plc's first quarter tumbled 77 percent to 70.8 million baht.

Thailand's finance sector is going through a major restructuring as authorities try to bail out the companies which have suffered from a crisis of confidence, lack of liquidity and an overall slowdown in the economy.
Analysts said they had expected finance firms to report poor first quarter results because trading gains were much lower than the large gains reported in the first quarter last year.
Trading volumes have also dropped 44 percent in the quarter compared to the same period last year, and the SET index fell nearly 47 percent from January 1, 1996 to March 31, 1997.
General Finance and Securities Plc surprised some by showing red ink this quarter, broker said. The company attributed its poor results to the slump in the market.
"The first quarter of 1997 has been a difficult quarter for all Thailand's finance and securities companies," Suchartchandra Pravitra, chairman and chief executive of General Finance, said.

He said General Finance, which reported a first quarter loss of 74.83 million baht compared to a 209.99 million baht net the same period in 1996, had been hurt by high cost of funds and deteriorating quality of loans as the Thai economy slowed.
